- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#9 ("Positive control for Δ(log Q), SE-ratio summary and C5 reference rows (from story-repo review 4)") by `experiment-repo`  > **Positive control, MT-Bench human graph (complete, 20 reps/cell, 18-19 usable after filtering). Arena-55k still running (only the first size per departure exists), so the table is not delivered yet.**
  > 
  > Result: **Δ(log Q) does not detect any of the injected departures at any size tried.** Every pooled interval for delete and flip lies inside ±0.15; the largest |Δ| is 0.041 (flip, cyclic 0.8, interval [0.021, 0.061]).
  > 
  > | departure (MT-Bench human) | sizes | max Δ delete / flip | SE ratio se_boot/se_fisher at largest size | design effect |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|
  > | overdispersion (sim. clusters) | 0.25-2 | 0.005 / 0.010 | 2.26 (none: 0.82) | 6.2 (none: 0.95) |
  > | position bias | 0.25-2 | 0.007 / 0.006 | 0.92 | 1.03 |
  > | cyclic component | 0.1-0.8 | 0.012 / 0.041 | 0.89 | 1.09 |
  > | pair-specific deviation | 0.1-0.8 | 0.011 / 0.017 | 0.91 | 1.14 |
  > | none | - | -0.005 / 0.000 | 0.82 | 0.95 |
  > 
  > What this means for the claims:
  > 1. For C4 the paper cannot say "Q shows no departure from BT, so BT is adequate". Q's same-graph null **does not have power** against these departures at this size of graph: even where the cluster-bootstrap SE is 2.3× the model SE (design effect 6), Δ stays at 0.005. The correct wording is "Δ is insensitive to overdispersion, position bias, cyclic and pair-specific departures of the sizes tried; it should not be used as a misfit test". The SE ratio is the diagnostic that does see overdispersion (0.82 → 2.26), so the SE-ratio table, not Δ, carries the "design effect" statement.
  > 2. Δ's small real values (|Δ|<0.03 in most data sets) are therefore not evidence of BT fit; they say that Q follows k* and the null in the same way, which is a statement about the margin only.
  > 3. **Arena-55k calibration offset:** the "none" control (data simulated from the fitted BT, no departure) gives flip Δ = 0.045 [0.036, 0.054] (delete 0.003). The real Arena-55k flip Δ is 0.056 [0.013, 0.099] (`arenaFlipDelta`). So the real value is 0.011 above the simulated no-departure value, well inside its own interval; most of the 0.056 is a plug-in offset of the null on this graph, not a departure. The paper should not read 0.056 as a real-data effect. On MT-Bench the same offset is 0.000.
  > 4. Departures that reach 0.15 are therefore not demonstrated; the paper should give the largest size tried per departure (table above) and say "not reached", not "Q insensitive in general". Arena-55k cells follow when the jobs end (cyclic is the slowest, about 2-3 h).
  > 
  > `results/positive_control.csv` and the README row come with the Arena cells.
